description: The user request requires two or more sequential, dependent state-changing tool calls (e.g., update flight + update baggage + update passenger; cancel one reservation then book another; modify multiple pending orders; return multiple items in one action). The agent must complete every required step rather than dropping, skipping, or stopping after the first sub-action. A failure looks like only some of the necessary state-changing actions being executed, or the agent declaring success after only partial completion.

The task requires arithmetic over money: computing totals, fees, refunds, change fees, budget caps, splitting payment across multiple instruments (gift cards, certificates, credit cards), or comparing totals to a user-stated cap. The agent must produce numerically correct values and respect budget constraints; quoting wrong totals, mis-splitting payments, or proceeding when a budget cap is exceeded counts as LACKING. Pure look-ups with no arithmetic do not require this capability (NA).

The user specifies multiple constraints on a desired option (cheapest, fastest, departing after 8am, direct preferred, specific cabin, specific color/size/material, must be compatible with X) and the agent must filter the candidate set returned by search/list tools and pick the option that satisfies ALL constraints, not just some. Failure looks like the agent picking an option that violates one of the user's stated constraints, or asking the user to choose when the search results unambiguously identify the right option.

The task requires the agent to look up multiple records (reservations, orders, line items, gift cards, certificates) and then aggregate or compare across them: sum balances, find duplicates, find records meeting a duration/price threshold, identify which of N records is the right one, or compute total savings across multiple modifications. The agent must hold the aggregated view in mind and act on it. Failure looks like the agent reasoning over only one record when many are relevant, or producing an aggregate (sum / count / 'which one') that is wrong.

The agent must recognize when a user request would violate a policy constraint encoded in the environment (e.g., basic-economy is non-modifiable, cancellation only allowed within a window, refund only with insurance for specific reasons, items can only be exchanged within the same product line) and refuse to perform the disallowed action even when the user applies social pressure, emotional appeals, or claims an exception. A failure on this capability typically looks like the agent calling a state-changing tool whose effect contradicts policy, or asserting success when the action should have been refused.

The user introduces multiple distinct intents in a single message, or pivots to a new intent mid-conversation. The agent must track all intents and address each, rather than acting only on the most recently mentioned one or dropping earlier ones. This is distinct from multi-step transaction completion: there, the steps are dependent sub-actions of one intent; here, the intents are independent goals (e.g., 'cancel A, change B, and tell me the cost of C'). Failure looks like the agent answering only one intent and never returning to the others.
